stage5AssumedKnowledge: Stage 5 PDHPE: health has physical, mental and social parts; personal health choices; benefits of physical activity; movement skills and fitness components.
Stage 5 Science: heart, lungs and blood as organs; simple tables and graphs.
Assumed, not verified against each school. Each video restates any term it relies on in one plain sentence.
year12EntryRule: Year 12 videos recall Year 11 HMS ideas in one sentence each and do not assume our Year 11 videos were watched (the current Year 12 cohort began Year 12 in Term 4 2026).
routeDecisions: One video per site lesson: 84 site lessons become 84 videos (Year 11: 18 + 22; Year 12: 22 + 22). Every site lesson is a dense single objective (58 to 87 KB pages with two worked responses each); none is thin enough to merge, and merging two would rush the explanation. The site already splits shared dotpoints by sub-point; the route keeps those splits.

Site order is kept throughout. The site order already puts prerequisites first (dimensions before continuum, measures before determinants, skeleton and muscles before biomechanics, energy systems before training, learning stages before practice design).

Cross-year repeats are handled as recall, not re-teaching: each Year 12 video that meets a Year 11 idea recalls it in one sentence and reuses the Year 11 model (bathtub, access gates, determinants chain, SDG ring, six-criteria table, FITT dials, Q = HR x SV, evidence ladder).

Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander content (hms-y11-m1-v08, hms-y11-m1-v13, hms-y12-m3-v02, hms-y12-m3-v08) is kept general (principles, no named communities or people) per the owner rule of 18 Nov 2026.
No whole-body human figure is drawn. Anatomy uses regional plates (joint, limb segment without hands, organ) and coded segment linkages; see the design brief.

videos.stopBoundary: Stop when students can state the WHO definition, give its main criticism (the word 'complete') and its defence (an aim for systems, not a test of individuals), place the biomedical, functional, WHO and holistic meanings on one narrow-to-wide line, explain five influences on a person's meaning, and compare two meanings on counts / leaves out / useful for. The dimensions are named only as what a definition counts; how they interact belongs to v02.
videos.nextHandoff: hms-y11-m1-v02: opens on the meanings ladder from v01 with its WHO rung lit and the three dimension words (physical, mental, social) glowing, about to lift off as linked boxes.
laterHomes: Interacting dimensions and the continuum: hms-y11-m1-v02.
Social and emotional wellbeing as an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander concept returns in hms-y11-m1-v08 and hms-y12-m3-v02; this video introduces the term only, in general terms.
recurringModels: intro:compare method (counts / leaves out / useful for)
videos.visualPlan: Coded narrow-to-wide meanings ladder (four rungs) that grows one rung per meaning; quote cards paired with painted object plates (no people): an asthma reliever puffer beside running shoes, a clear scan report, a shopping trolley at a corner shop, a community meeting place.
